message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium, 99.98 %), H‑2 (deuterium, 0.02 %), H‑3 (tritium, ~10⁻⁶ %) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | 53 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | 120 pm |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.452 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusion coefficient | ~0.0002 m² s⁻¹ (fastest among gases) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0016 mol L⁻¹) |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Polarity | Nonpolar |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (in acids, e.g., HCl), –1 (in hydrides, e.g., NaH) |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms acids, hydrides, and many organohydrogen compounds |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (pKa ≈ 35) in aqueous solution |
| | Redox behavior | Can act as both oxidizing and reducing agent depending on conditions |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, heavier, used in NMR, D₂O (“heavy water”) |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life ≈ 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion research |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (protium), 0 (deuterium), 2.978 µ_N (tritium) |
| | Binding energy per nucleon | ~1.1 MeV (protium), ~1.1 MeV (deuterium), ~1.1 MeV (tritium) |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industrial | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Scientific | Calibration gas, tracer studies, NMR spectroscopy (deuterium labeling) |
| | Energy | Potential clean energy carrier, hydrogen economy |
| | Medical | PET imaging (tritium-labeled compounds) |
| **Safety & Hazards** | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air |
| | Toxicity | Generally non‑toxic; inhalation of high concentrations can cause hypoxia |
| | Environmental impact | Low; does not produce greenhouse gases when combusted |

---

### Quick Reference Summary

- **Atomic number:** 1  
- **Molecular form:** H₂ (diatomic gas)  
- **Density:** 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (very light)  
- **Boiling point:** –252.9 °C (extremely low)  
- **Electronegativity:** 2.20 (moderate)  
- **Ionization energy:** 13.6 eV (high)  
- **Isotopes:** H‑1 (stable), H‑2 (stable, heavy water), H‑3 (radioactive, fusion)  

Hydrogen’s unique combination of low mass, high reactivity, and isotopic diversity makes it indispensable across chemistry, physics, industry, and emerging energy technologies.
